headline_marked: [[Intel ships first high-volume chips]] made with ASML's High NA EUV lithography
headline: Intel ships first high-volume chips made with ASML's High NA EUV lithography
summary: Intel's Panther Lake processors are the first to use this advanced lithography for high-volume production, with selected 18A layers dual-qualified for 0.55 NA scanners. This marks High NA EUV's transition from R&D to commercial deployment.
details: Intel is the first company to use ASML's High NA EUV lithography for high-volume logic chip manufacturing, specifically for selected layers of its Intel Core Ultra Series 3 "Panther Lake" processors. This significant milestone was announced by ASML, confirming Intel Foundry is utilizing the technology on its Intel 18A process node in Oregon.

High NA EUV extends semiconductor scaling by enabling smaller, denser circuit patterns, which were previously difficult to achieve with existing tools. Until now, this advanced platform was confined to R&D work, making this the first time it has produced and shipped a high-volume commercial logic product.

The technology increases the optical system's numerical aperture from 0.33 to 0.55, allowing for finer features in a single exposure and greater precision. This increased resolution is expected to reduce reliance on complex multi-patterning techniques, simplifying manufacturing and improving feature fidelity.

These capabilities are expected to support higher transistor densities and improved performance in future processors, particularly as AI workloads continue driving demand for advanced semiconductor technologies. Intel has been working with ASML for several years, installing one of the industry's first commercial High NA EUV systems, the TWINSCAN EXE:5000, and later qualifying the second-generation TWINSCAN EXE:5200B.

While High NA EUV is applied to specific layers, the remainder of the chip continues to be manufactured using conventional lithography. This approach mirrors how new lithography generations are typically introduced into advanced semiconductor production before broader adoption across future nodes, providing higher manufacturing output and flexibility.

headline_marked: [[Stripe and Advent reportedly offered to buy PayPal]] for around $53.4B
headline: Stripe and Advent reportedly offered to buy PayPal for around $53.4B
summary: A joint bid from Stripe and Advent International, reportedly backed by $50 billion in bank financing, aims to acquire PayPal. Both companies would hold equal stakes in the payments giant.
details: Stripe and private equity firm Advent International have reportedly submitted a joint bid to acquire PayPal, valued at approximately $53.4 billion. Reuters reports this offer was made earlier this month, backed by roughly $50 billion in committed bank financing.

Under the proposal, Stripe and Advent would jointly own PayPal, each holding an equal stake. This isn't the first time Stripe has been linked to a potential PayPal acquisition, with earlier reports in February suggesting preliminary discussions.

If completed, the deal would unite two major players in digital payments. PayPal serves around 440 million active accounts and handles $1.8 trillion in payment volume, while Stripe processes $1.9 trillion in payments.

The potential acquisition comes as PayPal faces significant changes, with new CEO Enrique Lores planning to cut at least $1.5 billion in costs. Reports also suggest a workforce reduction of around 20%.
Neither PayPal, Stripe, nor Advent International have publicly commented on the reported acquisition offer.
